summary: Lake Ontario island light off Prince Edward County: stone tower lit September 1856, keepers to 1919, 63-ft skeletal tower from 1959; island is a national wildlife area closed to landing.

lens.note: 360-degree French lens installed 1909 in place of the lamps and reflectors (Department report 1909-10). The optic after the 1919 acetylene light is not described in the sources read.

structures.note: 54 ft (LighthouseFriends). Register describes the stone building as ruins; the 1959 steel tower replaced its light.
63-ft skeletal tower; replaced the stone lighthouse which had started to crumble (LighthouseFriends)

structures.name: keeper's winter house, Nicholson Island
structures.note: Built on Nicholson Island for the keeper's winter accommodation (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Island is Scotch Bonnet Island National Wildlife Area. Visitation prohibited to protect nesting waterbirds (Register); access not permitted (LighthouseFriends). Distant view from near the end of Highway 20, west of Wellington.

events.note: Province of Canada Department of Public Works report asks for a light on Scotch Bonnet Island (LighthouseFriends)
Light House being built on Scotch Bonnet (Department of Public Works report 1853, as LighthouseFriends prints it)
Schooner Norfolk of Port Dover went ashore in a gale; captain and all hands (four) lost
Placed in operation September 1856 after the lighting apparatus was installed in the lantern room
Winter house built on Nicholson Island for the keeper
Lamps adapted to coal oil as whale oil became too expensive
New iron lantern placed atop the tower
Fourth-order 360-degree French lens with diamond vapour installation replaced the lamps and reflectors
Era of lightkeeping ends; acetylene light (acetylene compressed in acetone) installed in the lantern; foghorn discontinued; characteristic changed to one second visible, three seconds eclipsed
63-ft skeletal tower erected on the island, replacing the stone lighthouse which had started to crumble
Scotch Bonnet Island National Wildlife Area established to protect colonially nesting waterbirds

notes_for_editor: Whether the light is still lit is not settled by the sources read. The record says 'Sources differ on whether the light is still lit'. LighthouseFriends says lightkeeping ended in 1919 and the 1959 skeletal tower replaced the stone tower; it does not say the light went out. The record's CCG-derived characteristic (Fl W 4s) fits the 1919 description (one second visible, three eclipsed); the Coast Guard List of Lights was not read, so the story does not say whether it shows today. The 1854 Norfolk wreck rests on LighthouseFriends alone; a Chronicling America search for the island's name in 1853-1857 gave unrelated pages. Canadian newspapers were not searched. The Department of Public Works quotations for 1844 and 1853 are LighthouseFriends' and were not checked against the originals. Cyrus R. Spencer's date: the 1910-11 table reads 'April 7, 1903' with salary 425 by column position; the 1909-10 table (scan 178, printed 171) reads 'April 7, 1903' at $425 for the same row (checked on the page image, which corrects an earlier note that read it as 'Nov. 7, 1903'). The 1910-11 table (scan 269) reads the same (image checked). The 1912-13 table (scan 79, printed 72) lists C. R. Spencer at Scotch Bonnet with 'Apr. 27, 1903' and $520 (image checked), and the 1913-14 table (scan 84, printed 77) lists B. Y. Cunningham, appointed 'May 9, 1912', $440. The story states this disagreement about the handover. The Spencer date is the same person's, so one of the printed dates is an error; the story does not choose. The 1861 range (LighthouseFriends: 'thirteen-and-a-half miles') is printed as miles without a unit note and is left out of the story. The 2015 heritage designation in the record is not confirmed in the text the story quotes. The Parks Canada DFHD page returned only a shell in fetch_text, so the Register statement is from HistoricPlaces.ca. Keepers from 1896 onward rest on LighthouseFriends alone except Cyrus R. Spencer. Wrecks: the Norfolk wreck (November 1854) rests on LighthouseFriends alone; the story says so. Name variants and OCR-matched rows: Spencer and Cunningham were matched by column position in the Department tables; the images were checked for the 1909-10, 1910-11, 1912-13 and 1913-14 rows above. Harold Spencer (1919) was not checked.
